key_insight: A drilled-to-bossed joint geometry combined with optimized direct drive friction welding parameters substantially improves AA2024-T351 weld strength, while deep learning can predict tensile performance from process settings.
engineering_relevance: The study offers a practical route to stronger, more reliable lightweight aluminum joints for aerospace and automotive applications by coupling mechanical design with data-driven process optimization.
method: L18 orthogonal-array experiments on AA2024-T351 DDFW
Compared friction pressure, forging pressure, spindle speed, faying-surface geometry, and friction time
Trained deep learning models to predict ultimate tensile strength
evidence_signal: Under the best setting, the weld reached 538 MPa tensile strength and 325 MPa torsional strength, and the ensemble residual network achieved the strongest prediction performance with R² ≈ 0.81.
watch_item: The dataset appears limited to an L18 experimental design, so model generalization and transfer to other alloys, geometries, or welding setups may need further validation.
paper_title: Enhancing weld performance of AA2024-T351 using drilled-to-bossed geometry and deep learning prediction in direct drive friction welding
